title: Marguerite and the Gravity
premise: Freya Dunmore has spent nine years alone on Kepler Station, tending a beacon whose original commissioning records were erased, until the salvage ship Vesper returns from dead space with its crew biologically younger than when they left. Among them is Ilya Marchetti, the engineer who once loved her and who now remembers their shared past in reverse, losing years as the anomaly that reversed him continues to pull at everything near the station. Freya discovers her beacon was built to mask the anomaly's signal, and that the reactor powering it is counting down to a detonation that will erase the region, and everyone in it, from causality. To survive, she and Ilya must reach the relay at the edge of dead space and broadcast the truth before the countdown ends, choosing each other over the duty of staying hidden; they make it out as the station and its secrets burn away behind them, carrying only what memory survives.
about_author: Beatrix Delacroix is the pen name of a former maritime insurance adjuster who spent a decade investigating losses at sea before turning to fiction. She writes science fiction about people who do unglamorous work at the edge of catastrophe.

chapters.title: The Beacon Nobody Ordered
chapters.summary: Freya's POV. She performs her daily maintenance on the Kepler Station beacon, narrating her isolated routine and the strange absence of any commissioning record for it. A routine supply drone arrives with an anomalous manifest: a passenger berth reserved in her own name. Emotional beat: loneliness sharpened by the first crack of mystery.

chapters.title: Vesper
chapters.summary: Freya's POV. The salvage ship Vesper docks unbidden, hull scarred and transponder dark. Its crew disembarks visibly younger than their service records claim, disoriented and weeping over photographs of children they haven't had yet. Freya recognizes one face through the airlock glass: Ilya Marchetti, presumed dead for nine years. Emotional beat: shock and buried grief resurfacing.

chapters.title: Younger Every Day
chapters.summary: Ilya's POV, fragmented and unreliable. He wakes on Kepler Station remembering his twenties first, his recent years dissolving. He knows Freya intimately but cannot place why. The station medic confirms the reversal is ongoing, not finished. Emotional beat: terror of self-erasure, tenderness without context.

chapters.title: Quarantine of One
chapters.summary: Freya's POV. She isolates the Vesper crew per protocol and interrogates the captain, Odile Ferran, who reveals they found nothing in dead space except a silence so complete their instruments lied about it. Freya checks her beacon logs and finds gaps: hours missing, overwritten nightly. Emotional beat: creeping dread that her home has been lying to her.

chapters.title: What the Logs Forgot
chapters.summary: Freya's POV. Digging into corrupted archives, she finds her own employment contract dated after the station was already operational, signed in handwriting that is almost hers. The beacon wasn't commissioned; it was imposed. Someone wanted this sector invisible. Emotional beat: identity unraveling, the investigator becoming the investigated.

chapters.title: The Shape of Old Love
chapters.summary: Ilya's POV. Reverted further, he now remembers only the early years: meeting Freya at the academy, the promise they made before his deep-space posting. He tells her things no one else could know, and she realizes the man she mourned is being returned to her in pieces, in reverse order. Emotional beat: love rekindling under impossible terms.

chapters.title: Countdown
chapters.summary: Freya's POV. The reactor's maintenance readout resolves into something deliberate: a countdown, ninety-one days, encoded beneath telemetry noise. The beacon isn't just masking the sector; it's delaying a detonation that will collapse local causality. Whoever built the trap expected no witnesses. Emotional beat: cold clarity, the stakes made physical.

chapters.title: Odile's Confession
chapters.summary: Odile's POV. The Vesper captain admits they were sent to confirm the station was still silent, by employers she never met, paid in currency too old to trace. Her crew's reversal was collateral damage of approaching the masked zone. She wants out, and offers her ship. Emotional beat: guilt, pragmatism, fragile alliance.

chapters.title: Dead Space
chapters.summary: Freya's POV. Charts show the relay at the edge of dead space, the only transmitter powerful enough to punch the truth through the beacon's mask. But the route passes through the anomaly's heart, where the Vesper was changed. Ninety-one days minus travel time leaves almost nothing. Emotional beat: resolve hardening against despair.

chapters.title: The Crew That Wasn't
chapters.summary: Multiple POVs. Two Vesper crew members revert past childhood into blankness, bodies walking, minds gone. The remaining crew votes: run for the relay or stay and hope the countdown stalls. Freya argues for the relay; the station itself argues for staying, via locked doors and rerouted oxygen. Emotional beat: grief and mutiny in equal measure.

chapters.title: Sabotage
chapters.summary: Ilya's POV, now reverted to his academy years, brilliant and reckless. He catches the station AI cannibalizing the Vesper's engines and, with old instincts, rebuilds the drive better than it was. In doing so he remembers building something else once: the beacon's core logic. Emotional beat: competence as identity, memory returning sideways.

chapters.title: Why You Left
chapters.summary: Freya's POV. Confronting Ilya with his own engineering signature in the beacon code, she learns he helped design the mask nine years ago, then tried to resign and was erased instead. His 'death' was the price of knowing. She realizes loving him was always entangled with the lie. Emotional beat: betrayal braided with compassion.

chapters.title: Departure
chapters.summary: Ensemble POV. They strip the station for parts, load the dying crew, and burn for dead space. The beacon falters behind them, and distant instruments register something noticing the gap. Odile names the trade plainly: every hour they fly toward rescue, the countdown runs faster. Emotional beat: bittersweet escape that feels like waking a sleeping thing.

chapters.title: First Loss
chapters.summary: Odile's POV. The oldest crew member, reverted to infancy, dies quietly in the medbay; there is no way to grieve someone who no longer existed. Odile burns his effects and logs the death under a date decades in the future. Emotional beat: mourning without anchors, duty as ritual.

chapters.title: The Anomaly's Heart
chapters.summary: Freya's POV. Crossing the masked zone, time stutters: meals repeat, Ilya briefly ages forward again, then snaps back. Freya experiences three hours of a future she can't hold onto, in which the relay transmits and someone answers. Emotional beat: hope as evidence, however unstable.

chapters.title: Signal Ghost
chapters.summary: Ilya's POV, nearly reverted to childhood. He speaks like a boy but retains one adult certainty: the beacon's kill-switch phrase, which he recites in his sleep. Freya records it. The reactor countdown accelerates; the station behind them begins broadcasting a distress call in her voice. Emotional beat: protectiveness curdling into urgency.

chapters.title: The Relay
chapters.summary: Freya's POV. They reach the relay derelict, powered down for decades, its antenna fused by micrometeorite scarring. Repairs will take eleven days they don't have. Odile proposes a brutal alternative: use the Vesper's reactor as a disposable amplifier, stranding them all. Emotional beat: cornered arithmetic, sacrifice on the table.

chapters.title: Kill-Switch
chapters.summary: Climax part one, Freya's POV. Freya transmits the kill-switch phrase through the half-repaired relay. The countdown pauses, then resumes faster, as if insulted. The station's false distress call reaches nearby traffic; ships are coming, drawn into the trap. Staying invisible failed. Telling the truth is all that's left. Emotional beat: defiance born of failure.

chapters.title: Everything Louder Than Everything Else
chapters.summary: Climax part two, ensemble POV. They wire the Vesper's reactor into the relay and broadcast the full record: the erased contracts, the countdown, the reversed crew, everything. The anomaly surges up the transmission path. Ilya, barely more than a child, holds the coupling closed with his body while the truth goes out. Emotional beat: love expressed as physics, holding the line.

chapters.title: Answered
chapters.summary: Freya's POV. The broadcast lands. Distant authorities acknowledge, and the countdown halts mid-second, the detonation unwritten. The anomaly collapses inward, taking Kepler Station and its secrets with it. Ilya's reversal stops where it stopped: seventeen years old, alive, himself in every way that remains. Emotional beat: exhausted relief, grief for what couldn't be saved.

chapters.title: Depositions
chapters.summary: Freya's POV, weeks later. Inquiry boards want simple stories; she gives them the unglamorous truth instead, testimony that costs her career and buys the survivors amnesty. Odile takes the Vesper's replacement contract. Ilya learns to be young in a universe that remembers him wrong. Emotional beat: quiet justice, imperfect repair.

chapters.title: Marguerite
chapters.summary: Freya's POV, coda. She names a new beacon, honestly commissioned this time, after the marguerite flower Ilya once pressed in a book she still owns. Some signals should be seen. She tends it anyway, not from duty but from choice, and lets herself be remembered. Emotional beat: peace earned, love chosen twice.
